newsitem.title: USA: SBC to make another long-distance request.
newsitem.headline: SBC to make another long-distance request.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc plans to submit within 60 days an application to provide long-distance service in another of the seven states where it operates, Chief Executive Officer Edward Whitacre said.

Whitacre, speaking to Reuters after the company's annual meeting in San antonio, would not say in which state the application would be made, but when asked when it was likely to happen, he said, "Within the next 60 days."
Earlier on Friday, the Oklahoma Corporation Commission backed SBC Communications Inc application to provide long-distance phone service for customers there.
The commision's decision will now be forwarded to the Federal Communications Commission, which has final say in the matter.
If approved by the FCC, SBC would be the first Baby Bell allowed to enter the $80 billion long-distance business.

SBC officials welcomed the Oklahoma commission's vote and Whitacre played down complaints from competitors who oppose SBC's request to enter the long-distance market on the grounds that it has not opened up its local monopolies to competition.
"There are 90 companies approved to provide local service in our service area and they are doing it. If they say they are not, I can prove they are," he told Reuters.
"They don't want us to get long-distance approval because they think we'll be in the long-distance business and they have not come in to the local business in the size that they want," he said.
